title: Finite-level projection from the homotopy limit of strict adic cones
statement: Let R be a ring acting linearly on an abelian category A with its standard derived category [def-weil-abstract-derived-category] and countable products. A strict normalized adic tower is a functor U from the opposite natural numbers to unbounded cochain complexes of A, with an element v of R such that (1) v^j annihilates U_j, (2) for i <= j the map coker(v^i on U_j) -> U_i induced by the transition is a quasi-isomorphism, and (3) on U_(a+b), the image of v^a is the kernel of v^b for all natural a,b. For every natural k, form the tower of multiplication cones cone(v^k:U_(m+k)->U_(m+k)). If c is a homotopy-limit cone in the sense of the Roos distinguished triangle [def-weil-derived-limit], the map from c.pt to U_k given by its zeroth projection, the multiplication-cone cokernel augmentation and the normalized quotient comparison is an isomorphism. This includes k=0, where U_0 is zero.

proof.text: The exact multiplication sequence identifies the cokernel of the arrow-kernel inclusion in the mapping cone with U_k. The normalization quasi-isomorphism gives a distinguished triangle from the kernel complex to the multiplication cone to U_k. The identities defining kernels and cokernels make these triangles natural in the tower index.

source.place: Proof: coefficient triangles, nilpotent fibres, finite free tensor comparison and canonical maps

proof.text: The kernel transition over k steps is zero: on the kernel of v^k at index m+2k, exactness writes it as the image of v^(m+k); its reduction into index m+k is zero since v^(m+k) annihilates that level. Thus the kernel tower has nilpotent product shift, so the finite sum of its first k powers inverts one minus the shift. For k=0 all these kernels are zero.

source.place: Proof: coefficient triangles, nilpotent fibres, finite free tensor comparison and canonical maps

proof.text: Apply Hom into the tower triangles and the Roos triangle. The nilpotent kernel tower has zero homotopy limit; the constant U_k tower has homotopy limit U_k (finite partial sums split the difference map). Exactness therefore makes the displayed cone-limit projection invertible. This is the already proved source-library theorem; no proof is added or modified in that tree.
